page.layout: One column of running text, with three numbered entries, each headed by a title line. Left and right margins hold no printed notes; the cut-off fragments at the left edge belong to the neighbouring page. Running head at top centre, page number at top right, catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.head: Ruff. RHODON CYPARISSO. LXXI.
main_text.p: Lucanos iterum obveniffe dicunt. ideo abiecta falce, hastam & stimulum fabricabo, & artem bel-licam exercebo. non enim nos ociari patitur Deus: mihi hyeme æstas est gelidior. nam quid bello fit horridius? vere adueniente fleui. quam comatus ager stat floribus, quam odoratus a myrtis agellus, quam ornata spissa ista platanus? virct[?] triticum, omnia mihi ad abundantiam festinant. sed malum nobis dant hostes. exoptabilior enim iis ensis est aratro.
main_text.head: Amat. SOPATER TELESILLÆ. LXXII.
main_text.p: Nisi venereis voluptatibus invenustam satietatem miscuiffet natura, seruiret iam sexus masculus feminino, Telesilla. Non igitur superbias, mercatricula. Veneris mihi fax iam emortua est. neque dolores immortales amorum tela faciunt.
main_text.head: Eth. PROCLVS ARCHIMEDI. LXXIII.
main_text.p: Polypos dicunt in capturæ penuria, tricas fuas deuorare, membra fua nimirum miserrima, tanquam opsonium recuera[?] apparatum. Eduntigitur infelices membrorum suorum partes tenuissimas, & oftenduntur comedones esse propriæ carnis. Vt vero Xanthippe non omnibus habere polypi men-tem videaris, saltem fane ego illud esse creado certis-simum. Tractas enim nimis inhumaniter tuum pa-trem, neque naturam veritus, neq; poenam, quem-admodum barathrum timeri solet metuens. Sed si quidem refipicas, immemorem præteritorum ma-

page.notes: Ruff. and Amat. are abbreviations as I read them; Amat. is uncertain. "recuera" in the Procl. entry is uncertain (possibly "recuerat"). "virct" is probably "virct" as printed, with possible misprint for "virct"/"viret". Greek-letter abbreviation "Eth." is uncertain. Left-edge fragments are from the neighbouring page and were omitted. Spellings with ff and long s were copied as printed, with long s written as s.
